items.about: How each held picture (assets/sheets/map-held.json, frame held-<key>) is carried. len: length as a share of the figure's standing height (meta.stand). hand: the hand that holds it. grip: where the fist closes, as a share of the picture's height from its top (tip) end. two: two-handed. carry: handled (through the fist), strapped (on the forearm), book (in the hand by its top edge), palm (an orb held in the hand). style: the rest carry of a handled item (spec/held-items.md H5). offIdle: the style when carried in the off hand at rest. keepWorn: keeps its painted colours when Worn (tier 0).

grip.about: Shares of the cell (128 px) unless named otherwise.

hand-scan.about: How the painted hand is found over an orb or tome (spec H17). Distances are shares of the cell; colour distance is in 0-255 RGB.

row-swing.about: Tip angle on each of the nine steps of an added melee row, degrees (0 at the target, -90 up); null keeps the holding rule. heavyl is the heavy row drawn with the left hand uppermost.

worn-tint.about: Worn (tier 0) gear is dulled: saturation pulled toward grey by desaturate, then darkened by dim. Other tiers draw as painted.

enchant-glow.about: An enchanted handled item glows in its element's colour; blur as a share of the standing height, at least minPx screen px. Not drawn until items carry an enchantment.

clip-rows.about: The sheet row each action plays. melee and walk by what the main hand holds (fist: bare hands or no held picture); a sheet without the row plays the action's own row. An underwear (-unclad) look always uses fist; a tourist's melee with no held picture uses fist.

clip-holds.about: How long each of the nine steps shows, in 99ths of the clip (the clip's length is clipMs x the action row's frame count, data/ui.json). Rows not named take their action's list; a row with no list plays one frame per clipMs. melee (Justin 2026-10-19, a slight pause after the wind-up and the swing for emphasis): the top of the wind-up holds 95 ms and the strike 150 ms, the launch still at 170 ms (1.7 was 11, 13, 10, 7, 7, 24, 9, 9, 9).

clip-steps.about: The frame each step shows where it is not the step's own number. off: the off-hand jab of a dual wield (on the punch row).

old-death.about: A look with no death2 row plays its own death row by this frame list (the death holds above): the fall starts on the look's first falling frame.

walk.about: The run row is nine frames to two steps: framesPerStep frames a step, never faster than minFrameMs a frame. A step that starts within one step's time of the last one's end carries on the stride from the next whole frame.
